breakdown.description: 300 nm light has photon energy of about 4.13 eV, below a work function of 4.8 eV, so photoemission cannot occur.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly identified that 300 nm light (4.13 eV) is below the 4.8 eV work function and emission cannot occur, but it failed to resolve the inconsistency as the ground truth does — by replacing 300 nm with 240 nm (≈5.17 eV), where emission does occur with nonzero kinetic energy (~0.37 eV). The agent retained the incorrect wavelength and simply flagged the contradiction, rather than aligning with the ground truth's corrected scenario.
